using Dagger, LinearAlgebra

# A function can mutate its argument; the trailing ! is only a convention.
scale!(A::AbstractMatrix, alpha) = (A .*= alpha; A)

# Multiple dispatch chooses the method from the argument types.
describe(x::Number) = "a number"
describe(x::AbstractArray) = "an array with $(length(x)) elements"

# A do block passes its function as the first argument. Dagger's
# `spawn_datadeps() do ... end` uses the same syntax.
with_column(f, A) = f(@view A[:, 1])

function tour_of_julia()
    A = reshape(collect(1.0:12.0), 3, 4)

    # (1) Dispatch: the same name, a different method per argument type.
    println("describe(A) = ", describe(A))
    println("describe(3.5) = ", describe(3.5))

    # (2) Broadcasting applies an operation elementwise; the dot before `=`
    #     mutates in place. This is how tile kernels update whole arrays.
    B = scale!(copy(A), 2)
    println("2 .* A = ", B)

    # (3) A view aliases its parent; copying a slice does not.
    col = @view A[:, 2]
    col .= 0
    println("after writing the view, A[:, 2] = ", A[:, 2])

    # (4) A do block, as in `Dagger.spawn_datadeps() do ... end`.
    column_sum = with_column(A) do column
        sum(column)
    end
    println("sum of column 1 via a do block = ", column_sum)

    # (5) A closure captures values from the surrounding scope.
    addn(n) = x -> x + n
    println("addn(10)(5) = ", addn(10)(5))

    # (6) A named tuple is convenient for task metadata.
    tile = (name = "tile-3", rows = 2:3)
    println("tile.name = ", tile.name, ", tile.rows = ", tile.rows)

    # (7) A for loop walks a range or any iterable; the tile demos use this
    #     shape to visit every tile of a DArray.
    range_sum = 0
    for i in 1:4
        range_sum += i
    end
    println("sum 1:4 = ", range_sum)

    # (8) Nested loops share one `for`; `enumerate` pairs an index with each
    #     item, as in `for (i, tile) in enumerate(DA.chunks)`.
    C = zeros(2, 3)
    for j in 1:3, i in 1:2
        C[i, j] = 10i + j
    end
    for (k, value) in enumerate([2.0, 3.0, 5.0])
        println("item ", k, " = ", value)
    end
    println("C = ", C)

    # (9) Macros transform code before it runs: `@views` makes slices views,
    #     `@.` turns a whole expression into broadcasting.
    @views begin
        firstrow = A[1, :]
        firstrow .= 1
    end
    @. B = B + 1
    println("after @views and @.: A[1, :] = ", A[1, :])
    println("B[1, 1] after @. = ", B[1, 1])

    # (10) A preview of Dagger: `@spawn` returns a task, `fetch` waits for it.
    task = Dagger.@spawn sum(A)
    println("first Dagger task result = ", fetch(task))
end

using Dagger

# Report which thread ran the task (the sleep makes the overlap visible).
whereami() = (sleep(0.1); Threads.threadid())

function run_tasks()
    # (1) Spawn tasks. Passing a task as an argument makes a dependency, so
    #     `c` waits for `a` and `b` with no explicit synchronization.
    a = Dagger.@spawn rand(2000, 2000)
    b = Dagger.@spawn rand(2000, 2000)
    c = Dagger.@spawn a * b
    d = Dagger.@spawn sum(c)
    println("sum = ", fetch(d))

    # (2) Independent tasks run in parallel across threads. `Dagger.@spawn`
    #     takes a function call, so wrap multi-step work in a function.
    tids = fetch.([Dagger.@spawn whereami() for _ in 1:8])
    println("ran on threads: ", tids)
end

using Dagger

# Small tile operations; the ! means they mutate their first argument.
add!(X, Y) = (X .+= Y; nothing)
double!(X) = (X .*= 2; nothing)

function run_datadeps()
    # (1) Order follows the data: `copyto!` reads B, so it waits for `add!`.
    A = rand(1000); B = rand(1000); C = zeros(1000)
    B0 = copy(B)
    Dagger.spawn_datadeps() do
        Dagger.@spawn add!(InOut(B), In(A))      # B += A
        Dagger.@spawn copyto!(Out(C), In(B))     # C = B
    end
    ordered = C ≈ B0 .+ A
    println("ordered correctly: ", ordered)
    @assert ordered
    # Delete every `Dagger.@spawn` and In/Out/InOut wrapper: this is still
    # correct serial code. Datadeps keeps the program's sequential meaning.

    # (2) Parallelism comes from independent data. A DArray is a grid of
    #     tiles: 16 tiles give 16 independent tasks.
    DA = DArray(rand(4096, 4096), Blocks(1024, 1024))
    A0 = collect(DA)
    Dagger.spawn_datadeps() do
        for tile in DA.chunks
            Dagger.@spawn double!(InOut(tile))
        end
    end
    doubled = collect(DA) ≈ 2 .* A0
    println("16 tiles doubled in parallel: ", doubled)
    @assert doubled
end

using Dagger, CUDA, LinearAlgebra

# The same tile operation as the CPU demo.
double!(X) = (X .*= 2; nothing)

function run_gpu()
    # (1) Choose the GPU scope: every task spawned inside runs on one GPU.
    gpu = Dagger.scope(cuda_gpu=1)

    Dagger.with_options(scope=gpu) do
        # (2) Tile the array and double every tile; this is demo 2, unchanged.
        DA = DArray(rand(4096, 4096), Blocks(1024, 1024))
        A0 = collect(DA)
        Dagger.spawn_datadeps() do
            for tile in DA.chunks
                Dagger.@spawn double!(InOut(tile))
            end
        end
        doubled = collect(DA) ≈ 2 .* A0
        println("doubled on GPU: ", doubled)
        @assert doubled
        println("inside a GPU task, a tile is a ", fetch(Dagger.@spawn typeof(DA.chunks[1, 1])))

        # (3) Library code built on Datadeps works too: DArray matmul, now on
        #     the GPU.
        DC = DA * DA
        host_A = collect(DA)
        product_correct = collect(DC) ≈ host_A * host_A
        println("GPU matmul correct: ", product_correct)
        @assert product_correct
    end
end

using Dagger, LinearAlgebra, Random, CUDA

function run_product()
    ngpus = gpu_count()
    bs = 512

    # (1) One scope per GPU, and one scope that spans all of them.
    scopes = [Dagger.scope(cuda_gpu=g) for g in 1:ngpus]
    all_gpus = Dagger.scope(cuda_gpus=1:ngpus)

    # (2) A holds one tile per GPU; B is a single tile.
    A = rand(Xoshiro(1), bs * ngpus, bs)
    B = rand(Xoshiro(2), bs, bs)

    C = Dagger.with_options(scope=all_gpus) do
        DA = DArray(A, Blocks(bs, bs))
        DB = DArray(B, Blocks(bs, bs))
        DC = DArray(zeros(bs * ngpus, bs), Blocks(bs, bs))

        # (3) C[i] <- A[i] * B, with tile i pinned to GPU i.
        Dagger.spawn_datadeps() do
            for (i, gpu) in enumerate(scopes)
                Dagger.@spawn scope=gpu mul!(Out(DC.chunks[i, 1]), In(DA.chunks[i, 1]), In(DB.chunks[1, 1]))
            end
        end
        collect(DC)
    end

    @assert C ≈ A * B
    println("PASS: C ≈ A * B on $ngpus GPUs")
    return scopes
end

using Dagger, MPI, LinearAlgebra, Random

# Every rank runs this same program; `rank` says which one we are.
Dagger.accelerate!(:mpi)
const rank = MPI.Comm_rank(MPI.COMM_WORLD)
const ranks = MPI.Comm_size(MPI.COMM_WORLD)
BLAS.set_num_threads(1)   # one BLAS thread per process

function run_product()
    bs = 512

    # (1) One scope per rank, and one scope that spans all of them.
    scopes = [Dagger.constrain(Dagger.scope(mpi_rank=r), Dagger.DefaultScope())
              for r in 0:ranks-1]
    all_ranks = Dagger.constrain(Dagger.scope(mpi_ranks=:), Dagger.DefaultScope())

    # (2) A holds one tile per rank; B is a single tile.
    A = rand(Xoshiro(1), bs * ranks, bs)
    B = rand(Xoshiro(2), bs, bs)

    C = Dagger.with_options(scope=all_ranks) do
        DA = DArray(A, Blocks(bs, bs))
        DB = DArray(B, Blocks(bs, bs))
        DC = DArray(zeros(bs * ranks, bs), Blocks(bs, bs))

        # (3) C[i] <- A[i] * B, with tile i pinned to rank i-1.
        Dagger.spawn_datadeps() do
            for (i, owner) in enumerate(scopes)
                Dagger.@spawn scope=owner mul!(Out(DC.chunks[i, 1]), In(DA.chunks[i, 1]), In(DB.chunks[1, 1]))
            end
        end
        collect(DC)
    end

    @assert C ≈ A * B
    rank == 0 && println("PASS: C ≈ A * B on $ranks ranks")
    return scopes
end

using Dagger, MPI, CUDA, LinearAlgebra, Random

# Every rank runs this same program; `rank` says which one we are.
Dagger.accelerate!(:mpi)
const rank = MPI.Comm_rank(MPI.COMM_WORLD)
const ranks = MPI.Comm_size(MPI.COMM_WORLD)
const ngpus = 1   # GPUs per rank

function run_product()
    bs = 512

    # (1) One scope per (rank, GPU) pair, and one scope that spans all GPUs.
    scopes = [Dagger.scope(mpi_rank=r, cuda_gpu=g) for r in 0:ranks-1 for g in 1:ngpus]
    all_gpus = Dagger.scope(cuda_gpus=1:ngpus)

    # (2) A holds one tile per (rank, GPU) pair; B is a single tile.
    A = rand(Xoshiro(1), bs * length(scopes), bs)
    B = rand(Xoshiro(2), bs, bs)

    C = Dagger.with_options(scope=all_gpus) do
        DA = DArray(A, Blocks(bs, bs))
        DB = DArray(B, Blocks(bs, bs))
        DC = DArray(zeros(bs * length(scopes), bs), Blocks(bs, bs))

        # (3) C[i] <- A[i] * B, with tile i pinned to its own rank and GPU.
        Dagger.spawn_datadeps() do
            for (i, gpu) in enumerate(scopes)
                Dagger.@spawn scope=gpu mul!(Out(DC.chunks[i, 1]), In(DA.chunks[i, 1]), In(DB.chunks[1, 1]))
            end
        end
        collect(DC)
    end

    @assert C ≈ A * B
    rank == 0 && println("PASS: C ≈ A * B on $ranks ranks x $ngpus GPU per rank")
    return scopes
end

using Dagger, CUDA, Random
import Dagger: @stencil, Wrap

function run_stencil()
    # (1) A noisy 1024 x 1024 image, tiled 4 x 4. Each tile is one task.
    image = rand(Xoshiro(1), 1024, 1024)
    A = DArray(copy(image), Blocks(256, 256))
    B = zeros(Blocks(256, 256), 1024, 1024)

    # (2) Every pixel becomes the mean of its 3 x 3 neighbourhood. A pixel on
    #     a tile edge reads its neighbours from the next tile; Wrap() makes the
    #     image periodic, so the outer edges wrap around.
    @stencil B[idx] = sum(@neighbors(A[idx], 1, Wrap())) / 9
    box = sum(circshift(image, (i, j)) for i in -1:1, j in -1:1) / 9
    println("3x3 mean matches circshift: ", collect(B) ≈ box)

    # (3) Index the neighbourhood: nb[2, 2] is the pixel, nb[2, 1] and
    #     nb[2, 3] its neighbours along the second index.
    @stencil B[idx] = begin
        nb = @neighbors(A[idx], 1, Wrap())
        (nb[2, 3] - nb[2, 1]) / 2
    end
    slope = (circshift(image, (0, -1)) - circshift(image, (0, 1))) / 2
    println("centred difference matches: ", collect(B) ≈ slope)

    # (4) The statements of a block run in order, each over every tile: smooth
    #     into B, then copy B back into A. Ten passes blur the noise away.
    for _ in 1:10
        @stencil begin
            B[idx] = sum(@neighbors(A[idx], 1, Wrap())) / 9
            A[idx] = B[idx]
        end
    end
    println("pixel range: ", extrema(image), " before, ", extrema(collect(A)), " after 10 passes")

    # (5) The same stencil on the GPU: only the scope changes.
    Dagger.with_options(scope=Dagger.scope(cuda_gpu=1)) do
        G = DArray(copy(image), Blocks(256, 256))
        H = zeros(Blocks(256, 256), 1024, 1024)
        @stencil H[idx] = sum(@neighbors(G[idx], 1, Wrap())) / 9
        println("3x3 mean on the GPU matches: ", collect(H) ≈ box)
        println("inside a GPU task, a tile is a ", fetch(Dagger.@spawn typeof(H.chunks[1, 1])))
    end
end
